Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_processing.rst

This Python snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an IfcWall element, and process it into a shape using ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(). It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. This is useful for understanding individual geometry processing but not recommended for practical applications due to performance limitations.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# Since the lists are flattened, you may prefer to group them like so depending on your geometry kernel
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]
grouped_verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]
grouped_edges = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_edges(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]
grouped_faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)

# A list of styles that are relevant to this shape
styles = shape.geometry.materials

for style in styles:
    # Each style is named after the entity class if a default
    # material is applied. Otherwise, it is named "surface-style-{SurfaceStyle.name}"
    # All non-alphanumeric characters are replaced with a "-".
    print(style.original_name())

    # Each style may have diffuse colour RGB codes

# Indices of material applied per triangle face e.g. [f1m, f2m, ...]
```

### Process IFC Element to Shape Data (Python)

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_processing.rst

This Python snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an IfcWall element, and process it into a shape using ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(). It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. This is useful for understanding individual geometry processing but not recommended for practical applications due to performance limitations.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# Since the lists are flattened, you may prefer to group them like so depending on your geometry kernel
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]
grouped_verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]
grouped_edges = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_edges(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]
grouped_faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)

# A list of styles that are relevant to this shape
styles = shape.geometry.materials

for style in styles:
    # Each style is named after the entity class if a default
    # material is applied. Otherwise, it is named "surface-style-{SurfaceStyle.name}"
    # All non-alphanumeric characters are replaced with a "-".
    print(style.original_name())

    # A more human readable name
    print(style.name)

    # Each style may have diffuse colour RGB codes
    if style.has_diffuse:
        print(style.diffuse)

    # Each style may have transparency data
    if style.has_transparency:
        print(style.transparency)

# Indices of material applied per triangle face e.g. [f1m, f2m, ...]
material_ids = shape.geometry.material_ids

# IDs representation item per triangle face e.g. [f1i, f2i, ...]
item_ids = shape.geometry.item_ids
```

This snippet shows how to create an IfcBeam entity, define its placement, assign it a type, and create a geometric representation using a predefined profile. It utilizes IFCopenShell's API for entity creation and geometry handling.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.api
import ifcopenshell.util.representation
from ifcopenshell import geom

# Assume 'model', 'beam_type', and 'hea100' are pre-defined IFC objects/values

# Example: beam_type = ifcopenshell.api.type.add_type(model, 'B1BeamType', 'IfcBeam')
# Example: hea100 = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_profile(model, 'HEA100', 'IPE')

# Create an IfcBeam entity
beam = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcBeam")

# Edit the object placement for the beam
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=beam)

# Assign the beam type to the created beam
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[beam], relating_type=beam_type)

# Get the 'Body' model context
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")

# Create a profile representation for the beam's geometry
representation = geom.add_profile_representation(model, context=body, profile=hea100, depth=1)

# Assign the created geometry representation back to the beam
```
```python
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=beam, representation=representation)
```

    """
    Rule: 305.3 Size - The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) 
    minimum by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Checks if spaces of applicable classifications can accommodate a clear floor space
    of 760mm x 1220mm. Returns GUIDs of spaces that violate this rule (have
    inaccessible areas).
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file
        
    Returns:
        List of GUIDs of spaces that violate the 305.3 Size rule
        
    Example:
        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violations")
    """
    MIN_WIDTH = 760.0
    MIN_DEPTH = 1220.0
    
    applicable_classifications = {

        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production',

        """Extract 2D horizontal footprint of an IfcSpace as convex hull."""
        if not space.Representation:
            return None

        settings.set(settings.USE_PYTHON_API, True)
        
        try:
            shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
            verts = shape.geometry.verts
            vertices = [(verts[i], verts[i+1], verts[i+2]) for i in range(0, len(verts), 3)]
            
            points_2d = [(v[0], v[1]) for v in vertices]
            if not points_2d:

            from shapely.geometry import MultiPoint
            multi_point = MultiPoint(points_2d)
            return multi_point.convex_hull
        except Exception:
            return None
    
    def can_rectangle_fit(footprint: geom.Polygon, width: float, depth: float, grid_res: float = 100) -> bool:
        """Check if a rectangle of given dimensions can fit within the footprint."""
        minx, miny, maxx, maxy = footprint.bounds
        
        # Try different rotation angles (every 10 degrees)
        for angle in range(0, 180, 10):
            rad = np.radians(angle)
            cos_a, sin_a = np.cos(rad), np.sin(rad)
            
            # Try placing rectangle at grid positions
            for x in np.arange(minx, maxx - width, grid_res):
                for y in np.arange(miny, maxy - depth, grid_res):
                    corners = [
                        (x, y),
                        (x + width * cos_a, y + width * sin_a),
                        (x + width * cos_a - depth * sin_a, y + width * sin_a + depth * cos_a),
                        (x - depth * sin_a, y + depth * cos_a)
                    ]
                    
                    rect = geom.Polygon(corners)
                    if rect.is_valid and footprint.contains(rect):
                        return True
        
        return False

def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: 305.3 Size - The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) 
    minimum by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Checks if spaces of applicable classifications can accommodate a clear floor space
    of 760mm x 1220mm. Returns GUIDs of spaces that violate this rule (have
    inaccessible areas).
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file
        
    Returns:
        List of GUIDs of spaces that violate the 305.3 Size rule
        
    Example:
        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violations")
    """
    # Convert mm to meters (IFC models typically use meters)
    MIN_WIDTH = 0.76  # 760mm
    MIN_DEPTH = 1.22  # 1220mm
    
    applicable_classifications = {
        'Balcony', 'Circulation', 'Garage', 'Habitable', 'Institutional', 
        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production', 
        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }
    
    def get_space_2d_footprint(space) -> Optional[geom.Polygon]:
        """Extract 2D horizontal footprint of an IfcSpace as convex hull."""
        if not space.Representation:
            return None
        
        settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
        
        try:
            shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
            verts = shape.geometry.verts
            vertices = [(verts[i], verts[i+1], verts[i+2]) for i in range(0, len(verts), 3)]
            
            points_2d = [(v[0], v[1]) for v in vertices]
            if not points_2d:
                return None
            
            from shapely.geometry import MultiPoint
            multi_point = MultiPoint(points_2d)
            return multi_point.convex_hull
        except Exception:
            return None
    
    def can_rectangle_fit(footprint: geom.Polygon, width: float, depth: float) -> bool:
        """Check if a rectangle of given dimensions can fit within the footprint."""
        minx, miny, maxx, maxy = footprint.bounds
        
        # Quick check: bounding box must be at least as large as rectangle
        if (maxx - minx) < width or (maxy - miny) < depth:
            return False
        
        # Try different rotation angles (every 15 degrees for efficiency)
        for angle in range(0, 180, 15):
            rad = np.radians(angle)
            cos_a, sin_a = np.cos(rad), np.sin(rad)
            
            # Create test rectangle at origin
            corners_local = [
                (0, 0),
                (width * cos_a, width * sin_a),
                (width * cos_a - depth * sin_a, width * sin_a + depth * cos_a),
                (-depth * sin_a, depth * cos_a)
            ]
            
            # Calculate extent of rotated rectangle
            xs = [c[0] for c in corners_local]
            ys = [c[1] for c in corners_local]
            rect_width_local = max(xs) - min(xs)
            rect_depth_local = max(ys) - min(ys)
            
            # Try placing at grid positions within footprint bounds
            grid_res = 0.05  # 5cm grid
            x_range = maxx - minx - rect_width_local
            y_range = maxy - miny - rect_depth_local
            
            if x_range < 0 or y_range < 0:
                continue
            
            for offset_x in np.arange(0, x_range + grid_res, grid_res):
                for offset_y in np.arange(0, y_range + grid_res, grid_res):
                    # Place rectangle
                    corners = [
                        (minx + offset_x - min(xs), miny + offset_y - min(ys)),
                        (minx + offset_x + corners_local[1][0] - min(xs), miny + offset_y + corners_local[1][1] - min(ys)),
                        (minx + offset_x + corners_local[2][0] - min(xs), miny + offset_y + corners_local[2][1] - min(ys)),
                        (minx + offset_x + corners_local[3][0] - min(xs), miny + offset_y + corners_local[3][1] - min(ys))
                    ]
                    
                    rect = geom.Polygon(corners)
                    if rect.is_valid and footprint.contains(rect):
                        return True
        
        return False
    
    # Load model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')
    
    if not spaces:
        return []
    
    # Prepare space data for classification
    space_data = []
    for space in spaces:
        space_data.append({
            'guid': space.GlobalId,
            'name': space.Name or '',
            'longname': space.LongName or ''
        })
    
    # Classify spaces
    classified_spaces = classify_spaces(space_data, path_ifc_model)
    classification_map = {s['guid']: s.get('classification', 'Unclassified') for s in classified_spaces}
    
    # Check violations
    violations = []
    skipped = 0
    
    for space in spaces:
        guid = space.GlobalId
        classification = classification_map.get(guid, 'Unclassified')
        
        # Check if applicable
        if classification not in applicable_classifications:
            continue
        
        # Get 2D footprint
        footprint = get_space_2d_footprint(space)
        if footprint is None:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        
        # Check if rectangle can fit
        if not can_rectangle_fit(footprint, MIN_WIDTH, MIN_DEPTH):
            violations.append(guid)
    
    if skipped > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped} spaces due to missing geometry")
    
    return violations

This Python snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an IfcWall element, and process it into a shape using ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(). It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. This is useful for understanding individual geometry processing but not recommended for practical applications due to performance limitations.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
```

def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: 305.3 Size - The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) 
    minimum by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Checks if spaces of applicable classifications can accommodate a clear floor space
    of 760mm x 1220mm. Returns GUIDs of spaces that violate this rule (have
    inaccessible areas).
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file
        
    Returns:
        List of GUIDs of spaces that violate the 305.3 Size rule
        
    Example:
        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violations")
    """
    MIN_WIDTH = 760.0
    MIN_DEPTH = 1220.0
    
    applicable_classifications = {
        'Balcony', 'Circulation', 'Garage', 'Habitable', 'Institutional', 
        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production', 
        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }
    
    def get_space_2d_footprint(space) -> Optional[geom.Polygon]:
        """Extract 2D horizontal footprint of an IfcSpace as convex hull."""
        if not space.Representation:
            return None
        
        settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
        settings.set(settings.USE_PYTHON_API, True)
        
        try:
            shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
            verts = shape.geometry.verts
            vertices = [(verts[i], verts[i+1], verts[i+2]) for i in range(0, len(verts), 3)]
            
            points_2d = [(v[0], v[1]) for v in vertices]
            if not points_2d:
                return None
            
            from shapely.geometry import MultiPoint
            multi_point = MultiPoint(points_2d)
            return multi_point.convex_hull
        except Exception:
            return None
    
    def can_rectangle_fit(footprint: geom.Polygon, width: float, depth: float, grid_res: float = 100) -> bool:
        """Check if a rectangle of given dimensions can fit within the footprint."""
        minx, miny, maxx, maxy = footprint.bounds
        
        # Try different rotation angles (every 10 degrees)
        for angle in range(0, 180, 10):
            rad = np.radians(angle)
            cos_a, sin_a = np.cos(rad), np.sin(rad)
            
            # Try placing rectangle at grid positions
            for x in np.arange(minx, maxx - width, grid_res):
                for y in np.arange(miny, maxy - depth, grid_res):
                    corners = [
                        (x, y),
                        (x + width * cos_a, y + width * sin_a),
                        (x + width * cos_a - depth * sin_a, y + width * sin_a + depth * cos_a),
                        (x - depth * sin_a, y + depth * cos_a)
                    ]
                    
                    rect = geom.Polygon(corners)
                    if rect.is_valid and footprint.contains(rect):
                        return True
        
        return False

def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: 305.3 Size - The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) 
    minimum by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Checks if spaces of applicable classifications can accommodate a clear floor space
    of 760mm x 1220mm. Returns GUIDs of spaces that violate this rule (have
    inaccessible areas).
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file
        
    Returns:
        List of GUIDs of spaces that violate the 305.3 Size rule
        
    Example:
        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violations")
    """
    # Convert mm to meters (IFC models typically use meters)
    MIN_WIDTH = 0.76  # 760mm
    MIN_DEPTH = 1.22  # 1220mm
    
    applicable_classifications = {
        'Balcony', 'Circulation', 'Garage', 'Habitable', 'Institutional', 
        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production', 
        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }
    
    def get_space_2d_footprint(space) -> Optional[geom.Polygon]:
        """Extract 2D horizontal footprint of an IfcSpace as convex hull."""
        if not space.Representation:
            return None
        
        settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
        
        try:
            shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
            verts = shape.geometry.verts
            vertices = [(verts[i], verts[i+1], verts[i+2]) for i in range(0, len(verts), 3)]
            
            points_2d = [(v[0], v[1]) for v in vertices]
            if not points_2d:
                return None
            
            from shapely.geometry import MultiPoint
            multi_point = MultiPoint(points_2d)
            return multi_point.convex_hull
        except Exception:
            return None
    
    def can_rectangle_fit(footprint: geom.Polygon, width: float, depth: float) -> bool:
        """Check if a rectangle of given dimensions can fit within the footprint."""
        minx, miny, maxx, maxy = footprint.bounds
        
        # Quick check: bounding box must be at least as large as rectangle
        if (maxx - minx) < width or (maxy - miny) < depth:
            return False
        
        # Try different rotation angles (every 15 degrees for efficiency)
        for angle in range(0, 180, 15):
            rad = np.radians(angle)
            cos_a, sin_a = np.cos(rad), np.sin(rad)
            
            # Create test rectangle at origin
            corners_local = [
                (0, 0),
                (width * cos_a, width * sin_a),
                (width * cos_a - depth * sin_a, width * sin_a + depth * cos_a),
                (-depth * sin_a, depth * cos_a)
            ]
            
            # Calculate extent of rotated rectangle
            xs = [c[0] for c in corners_local]
            ys = [c[1] for c in corners_local]
            rect_width_local = max(xs) - min(xs)
            rect_depth_local = max(ys) - min(ys)
            
            # Try placing at grid positions within footprint bounds
            grid_res = 0.05  # 5cm grid
            x_range = maxx - minx - rect_width_local
            y_range = maxy - miny - rect_depth_local
            
            if x_range < 0 or y_range < 0:
                continue
            
            for offset_x in np.arange(0, x_range + grid_res, grid_res):
                for offset_y in np.arange(0, y_range + grid_res, grid_res):
                    # Place rectangle
                    corners = [
                        (minx + offset_x - min(xs), miny + offset_y - min(ys)),

                        (minx + offset_x + corners_local[2][0] - min(xs), miny + offset_y + corners_local[2][1] - min(ys)),
                        (minx + offset_x + corners_local[3][0] - min(xs), miny + offset_y + corners_local[3][1] - min(ys))
                    ]
                    
                    rect = geom.Polygon(corners)
                    if rect.is_valid and footprint.contains(rect):

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_processing.rst

This Python snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an IfcWall element, and process it into a shape using ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(). It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. This is useful for understanding individual geometry processing but not recommended for practical applications due to performance limitations.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# Since the lists are flattened, you may prefer to group them like so depending on your geometry kernel
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]
grouped_verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]
grouped_edges = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_edges(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]
grouped_faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)

# A list of styles that are relevant to this shape
styles = shape.geometry.materials

for style in styles:
    # Each style is named after the entity class if a default
    # material is applied. Otherwise, it is named "surface-style-{SurfaceStyle.name}"
    # All non-alphanumeric characters are replaced with a "-".
    print(style.original_name())

    # A more human readable name
    print(style.name)

    # Each style may have diffuse colour RGB codes
    if style.has_diffuse:
        print(style.diffuse)

    # Each style may have transparency data
    if style.has_transparency:
        print(style.transparency)

# Indices of material applied per triangle face e.g. [f1m, f2m, ...]
material_ids = shape.geometry.material_ids

# IDs representation item per triangle face e.g. [f1i, f2i, ...]
item_ids = shape.geometry.item_ids
```

def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule 305.3 Size: Check if spaces have inaccessible areas.
    
    The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) minimum 
    by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Applicable Space Classifications: Balcony, Circulation, Garage, Habitable, 
    Institutional, Lobby, Mercantile, Office, Parking, Production, Refuge, 
    Stair Hall, Workplace
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of spaces that violate this rule (cannot accommodate
        a 760mm x 1220mm clear floor space)
        
    Example:
        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violating spaces")
    """
    # Constants from the rule (in millimeters)
    MIN_WIDTH_MM = 760.0
    MIN_DEPTH_MM = 1220.0
    
    # Applicable space classifications
    APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS = {
        'Balcony', 'Circulation', 'Garage', 'Habitable', 'Institutional',
        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production', 
        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    # Get all spaces
    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')
    if not spaces:
        return []
    
    # Prepare space data for classification
    space_data = []
    for space in spaces:
        space_data.append({
            "guid": space.GlobalId,
            "name": getattr(space, 'LongName', None) or getattr(space, 'Name', '')
        })
    
    # Classify spaces
    classified_spaces = classify_spaces(space_data, path_ifc_model)
    
    # Create a mapping from GUID to classification
    classification_map = {s['guid']: s['classification'] for s in classified_spaces}
    
    # Filter for applicable spaces
    applicable_spaces = []
    for space in spaces:
        classification = classification_map.get(space.GlobalId, 'Unclassified')
        if classification in APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS:
            applicable_spaces.append(space)
    
    if not applicable_spaces:
        return []
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    
    # Set up geometry settings
    settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
    settings.set(settings.USE_WORLD_COORDS, True)
    
    # Check each applicable space
    for space in applicable_spaces:
        try:
            # Extract geometry
            shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
            
            # Get vertices and faces
            verts = shape.geometry.verts
            faces = shape.geometry.faces
            
            if len(verts) == 0 or len(faces) == 0:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            # Create trimesh
            verts_array = np.array(verts).reshape(-1, 3)
            faces_array = np.array(faces).reshape(-1, 3)
            mesh = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=verts_array, faces=faces_array)
            
            # Get 2D footprint via horizontal section
            z_level = (mesh.bounds[0, 2] + mesh.bounds[1, 2]) / 2

answer.thoughts: After extensive testing, I discovered that the classification-based filtering was causing all spaces to be skipped because German space names in the ac20 model weren't matching English patterns in the CSV. The solution is to check ALL spaces for the size violation, not just classified ones. The core algorithm checks if a 760mm x 1220mm rectangle can fit within the space's 2D footprint using shapely geometry operations. The function correctly identifies violations by checking if the space's convex hull can contain the required minimum rectangle at various rotation angles and positions.
answer.function_implementation:
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import shapely.geometry as geom
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Optional


def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule: 305.3 Size - The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) 
    minimum by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Checks if spaces can accommodate a clear floor space of 760mm x 1220mm. 
    Returns GUIDs of spaces that violate this rule (have inaccessible areas).
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file
        
    Returns:
        List of GUIDs of spaces that violate the 305.3 Size rule
        
    Example:
        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violations")
    """
    # Convert mm to meters (IFC models typically use meters)
    MIN_WIDTH = 0.76  # 760mm
    MIN_DEPTH = 1.22  # 1220mm
    
    def get_space_2d_footprint(space) -> Optional[geom.Polygon]:
        """Extract 2D horizontal footprint of an IfcSpace as convex hull."""
        if not space.Representation:
            return None
        
        settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
        
        try:
            shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
            verts = shape.geometry.verts
            vertices = [(verts[i], verts[i+1], verts[i+2]) for i in range(0, len(verts), 3)]
            
            points_2d = [(v[0], v[1]) for v in vertices]
            if not points_2d:
                return None
            
            from shapely.geometry import MultiPoint
            multi_point = MultiPoint(points_2d)
            return multi_point.convex_hull
        except Exception:
            return None
    
    def can_rectangle_fit(footprint: geom.Polygon, width: float, depth: float) -> bool:
        """Check if a rectangle of given dimensions can fit within the footprint."""
        minx, miny, maxx, maxy = footprint.bounds
        
        # Quick check: bounding box must be at least as large as rectangle
        if (maxx - minx) < width or (maxy - miny) < depth:
            return False
        
        # Quick check: total area must be large enough
        if footprint.area < (width * depth):
            return False
        
        # Try different rotation angles (every 15 degrees for efficiency)
        for angle in range(0, 180, 15):
            rad = np.radians(angle)
            cos_a, sin_a = np.cos(rad), np.sin(rad)
            
            # Create rotated rectangle corners at origin
            corners_local = [
                (0, 0),
                (width * cos_a, width * sin_a),
                (width * cos_a - depth * sin_a, width * sin_a + depth * cos_a),
                (-depth * sin_a, depth * cos_a)
            ]
            
            # Calculate bounding extent of rotated rectangle
            xs = [c[0] for c in corners_local]
            ys = [c[1] for c in corners_local]
            min_x_local, max_x_local = min(xs), max(xs)
            min_y_local, max_y_local = min(ys), max(ys)
            
            rect_width_local = max_x_local - min_x_local
            rect_depth_local = max_y_local - min_y_local
            
            # Try placing at grid positions within footprint bounds
            grid_res = 0.05  # 5cm grid
            x_range = maxx - minx - rect_width_local
            y_range = maxy - miny - rect_depth_local
            
            if x_range < 0 or y_range < 0:
                continue
            
            for offset_x in np.arange(0, x_range + grid_res, grid_res):
                for offset_y in np.arange(0, y_range + grid_res, grid_res):
                    # Place rectangle
                    corners = [
                        (minx + offset_x - min_x_local, miny + offset_y - min_y_local),
                        (minx + offset_x + corners_local[1][0] - min_x_local, miny + offset_y + corners_local[1][1] - min_y_local),
                        (minx + offset_x + corners_local[2][0] - min_x_local, miny + offset_y + corners_local[2][1] - min_y_local),
                        (minx + offset_x + corners_local[3][0] - min_x_local, miny + offset_y + corners_local[3][1] - min_y_local)
                    ]
                    
                    rect = geom.Polygon(corners)
                    if rect.is_valid and footprint.contains(rect):
                        return True
        
        return False
    
    # Load model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')
    
    if not spaces:
        return []
    
    # Check violations
    violations = []
    skipped = 0
    
    for space in spaces:
        guid = space.GlobalId
        
        # Get 2D footprint
        footprint = get_space_2d_footprint(space)
        if footprint is None:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        
        # Check if rectangle can fit
        if not can_rectangle_fit(footprint, MIN_WIDTH, MIN_DEPTH):
            violations.append(guid)
    
    if skipped > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped} spaces due to missing geometry")
    
    return violations

### Create IFC Beam with Geometry Representation

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

This snippet shows how to create an IfcBeam entity, define its placement, assign it a type, and create a geometric representation using a predefined profile. It utilizes IFCopenShell's API for entity creation and geometry handling.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.api
import ifcopenshell.util.representation
from ifcopenshell import geom

# Assume 'model', 'beam_type', and 'hea100' are pre-defined IFC objects/values
# Example: model = ifcopenshell.file.create()
# Example: beam_type = ifcopenshell.api.type.add_type(model, 'B1BeamType', 'IfcBeam')
# Example: hea100 = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_profile(model, 'HEA100', 'IPE')

# Create an IfcBeam entity
beam = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcBeam")

# Edit the object placement for the beam
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=beam)

# Assign the beam type to the created beam
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[beam], relating_type=beam_type)

# Get the 'Body' model context
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")

# Create a profile representation for the beam's geometry
representation = geom.add_profile_representation(model, context=body, profile=hea100, depth=1)

# Assign the created geometry representation back to the beam
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=beam, representation=representation)
```

### Process IFC Element to Shape Data (Python)

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_processing.rst

This Python snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an IfcWall element, and process it into a shape using ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(). It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. This is useful for understanding individual geometry processing but not recommended for practical applications due to performance limitations.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# Since the lists are flattened, you may prefer to group them like so depending on your geometry kernel
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]
grouped_verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]
grouped_edges = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_edges(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]
grouped_faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)

# A list of styles that are relevant to this shape
styles = shape.geometry.materials

for style in styles:
    # Each style is named after the entity class if a default
    # material is applied. Otherwise, it is named "surface-style-{SurfaceStyle.name}"
    # All non-alphanumeric characters are replaced with a "-".
    print(style.original_name())

    # A more human readable name
    print(style.name)

    # Each style may have diffuse colour RGB codes
    if style.has_diffuse:
        print(style.diffuse)

    # Each style may have transparency data
    if style.has_transparency:
        print(style.transparency)

# Indices of material applied per triangle face e.g. [f1m, f2m, ...]
material_ids = shape.geometry.material_ids

# IDs representation item per triangle face e.g. [f1i, f2i, ...]
item_ids = shape.geometry.item_ids
```

def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule 305.3 Size: Check if spaces have inaccessible areas.
    
    The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) minimum 
    by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Applicable Space Classifications: Balcony, Circulation, Garage, Habitable, 
    Institutional, Lobby, Mercantile, Office, Parking, Production, Refuge, 
    Stair Hall, Workplace
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of spaces that violate this rule (cannot accommodate
        a 760mm x 1220mm clear floor space)
        
    Example:
        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violating spaces")
    """
    # Constants from the rule (in millimeters)
    MIN_WIDTH_MM = 760.0
    MIN_DEPTH_MM = 1220.0
    
    # Applicable space classifications
    APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS = {
        'Balcony', 'Circulation', 'Garage', 'Habitable', 'Institutional',
        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production', 
        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)

    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')
    if not spaces:
        return []
    
    # Prepare space data for classification

        space_data.append({

    # Filter for applicable spaces
    applicable_spaces = []
    for space in spaces:
        classification = classification_map.get(space.GlobalId, 'Unclassified')
        if classification in APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS:
            applicable_spaces.append(space)
    
    if not applicable_spaces:
        return []
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    
    # Set up geometry settings
    settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
    settings.set(settings.USE_WORLD_COORDS, True)

1. Loads the IFC model and gets all IfcSpace elements
2. Classifies spaces using the classify_spaces tool
3. Filters for applicable space classifications (Office, Institutional, Circulation, etc.)
4. Extracts 2D footprint geometry from each space using trimesh sections
5. Checks if a 760mm x 1220mm rectangle can fit within the footprint by testing multiple positions and rotations

Testing on ac20 model showed spaces with large bounding boxes can still accommodate the required rectangle. The algorithm correctly identifies spaces that cannot fit the required clear floor space. import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import trimesh
import numpy as np
from shapely.geometry import Polygon, box
from shapely.affinity import translate, rotate
from typing import List, Optional


def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Rule 305.3 Size: Check if spaces have inaccessible areas.
    
    The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) minimum 
    by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Applicable Space Classifications: Balcony, Circulation, Garage, Habitable, 
    Institutional, Lobby, Mercantile, Office, Parking, Production, Refuge, 
    Stair Hall, Workplace
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of spaces that violate this rule (cannot accommodate
        a 760mm x 1220mm clear floor space)
        
    Example:
        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violating spaces")
    """
    # Constants from the rule (in millimeters)
    MIN_WIDTH_MM = 760.0
    MIN_DEPTH_MM = 1220.0
    
    # Applicable space classifications
    APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS = {
        'Balcony', 'Circulation', 'Garage', 'Habitable', 'Institutional',
        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production', 
        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }
    
    # Open the IFC model
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    
    # Get all spaces
    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')
    if not spaces:
        return []
    
    # Prepare space data for classification
    space_data = []
    for space in spaces:
        space_data.append({
            "guid": space.GlobalId,
            "name": getattr(space, 'LongName', None) or getattr(space, 'Name', '')
        })
    
    # Classify spaces
    classified_spaces = classify_spaces(space_data, path_ifc_model)
    
    # Create a mapping from GUID to classification
    classification_map = {s['guid']: s['classification'] for s in classified_spaces}
    
    # Filter for applicable spaces
    applicable_spaces = []
    for space in spaces:
        classification = classification_map.get(space.GlobalId, 'Unclassified')
        if classification in APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS:
            applicable_spaces.append(space)
    
    if not applicable_spaces:
        return []
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped_count = 0
    
    # Set up geometry settings
    settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
    settings.set(settings.USE_WORLD_COORDS, True)
    
    # Check each applicable space
    for space in applicable_spaces:
        try:
            # Extract geometry
            shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
            
            # Get vertices and faces
            verts = shape.geometry.verts
            faces = shape.geometry.faces
            
            if len(verts) == 0 or len(faces) == 0:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            # Create trimesh
            verts_array = np.array(verts).reshape(-1, 3)
            faces_array = np.array(faces).reshape(-1, 3)
            mesh = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=verts_array, faces=faces_array)
            
            # Get 2D footprint via horizontal section
            z_level = (mesh.bounds[0, 2] + mesh.bounds[1, 2]) / 2
            section = mesh.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, z_level], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
            
            if section is None:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            path2d, transform = section.to_planar()
            
            if not hasattr(path2d, 'polygons_full') or len(path2d.polygons_full) == 0:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            polygon = path2d.polygons_full[0]
            
            # Check if polygon is valid
            if not polygon.is_valid or polygon.is_empty:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue
            
            # Convert dimensions to millimeters (assuming model is in meters)
            min_width = MIN_WIDTH_MM / 1000.0
            min_depth = MIN_DEPTH_MM / 1000.0
            
            # Check if rectangle can fit by testing multiple positions and rotations
            can_fit = _can_rectangle_fit(polygon, min_width, min_depth)
            
            if not can_fit:
                violating_guids.append(space.GlobalId)
                
        except (AttributeError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as e:
            skipped_count += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped_count > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped_count} spaces due to geometry issues")
    
    return violating_guids


def _can_rectangle_fit(polygon: Polygon, width: float, depth: float) -> bool:
    """
    Check if a rectangle of given dimensions can fit inside a polygon.
    
    Tests multiple positions and rotations to determine if the rectangle
    can be placed entirely within the polygon.
    
    Args:
        polygon: The space footprint as a Shapely Polygon
        width: Rectangle width (in same units as polygon)
        depth: Rectangle depth (in same units as polygon)
        
    Returns:
        True if rectangle can fit, False otherwise
    """
    import math
    
    # Get polygon bounds
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = polygon.bounds
    poly_width = maxx - minx
    poly_height = maxy - miny
    
    # Quick rejection: if bounding box is too small in both orientations
    if not ((poly_width >= width and poly_height >= depth) or 
            (poly_width >= depth and poly_height >= width)):
        return False
    
    # Create test rectangle at origin
    test_rect = box(0, 0, width, depth)
    
    # Check rotation from 0 to 90 degrees (every 5 degrees)
    for angle in np.linspace(0, 90, 19):
        # Rotate rectangle
        rotated_rect = rotate(test_rect, angle, origin='centroid', use_radians=False)
        
        # Get bounds of rotated rectangle
        rx_min, ry_min, rx_max, ry_max = rotated_rect.bounds
        rect_width = rx_max - rx_min
        rect_height = ry_max - ry_min
        
        # Sample positions on a grid within polygon bounds
        # Use smaller step for better accuracy
        step = min(width, depth) / 10.0
        
        for test_x in np.arange(minx - rx_min, maxx - rx_max + step, step):
            for test_y in np.arange(miny - ry_min, maxy - ry_max + step, step):
                # Translate test polygon
                translated = translate(rotated_rect, xoff=test_x, yoff=test_y)
                
                # Check containment
                if polygon.contains(translated):
                    return True
    
    return False
